chapter: Vegas groups and Spokane solo years
title: Regrouping for Las Vegas and Lee Dear's story
summary: New lineup with Tony Ardito and Joey Preston, the Thunderbird lounge, and owner Lee Dear who sent Charlie Parker to New York and rescued Joe Pass.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: And they were all very good players. Anyway when this group broke up we added another guitar player from the hometown but he was a pain in the neck and he was sort of a prima donna and that didn’t last long. So then we added two more guys and it just never felt right. So finally the group broke up and I had a chance to reorganize it so I got a trombone player from Scranton, Tony Ardito, he was a great player, and a guitar player from Coatesville, Pennsylvania that we had never heard before but he had a good name, and a drummer from Baltimore named Joey Preston. His real name was Joey Prestiani. But Joey was a child prodigy. When he was 14 he was playing with the Kenton band. I mean he was a brilliant, brilliant player. He did a lot of movies and he wore short pants when he was like 10 or 11 because he was small and got away with it. And this group came out here and we were killing them out here in Vegas. And then the guitar player, who was a lot older than us, he decided he didn’t want to travel anymore. So he stayed with one of the show bands and then we just worked as a trio without him and we added a local piano player and we were at the Thunderbird Hotel for a long time, we were sort of like the house group in the lounge there. And one of the owners of the Thunderbird was very fond of us. He was a guy who owned a club in Wichita many years ago and he bought into the Thunderbird but couldn’t be on the license because he had a felony conviction. But at his club in Wichita Charlie Parker used to work there and he was © Fillius Jazz Archive -9-

always getting in trouble because he’d go in the boiler room and smoke a joint and it would get into the ventilator. People would smell this weird smell. So Lee Dear was the man’s name I can tell you, he’s since passed away, he was a dear man. And he said to Charlie Parker, “You’ve got to get out of here, go to New York.” He later saved the life of maybe the best guitar player who ever lived, Joe Pass, who was a terrible user of hard drugs. And he took Joe Pass physically by the hand, took him out to the airport in Vegas, put him on a plane to Los Angeles to get in touch with Synanon, and told the flight attendant, “He’s not to leave the plane until Synanon comes on the plane.” This was the old days before security, and gets him and takes him. And anyway Joe Pass went into Synanon and straightened his life out and disappeared for a couple of years and then I had the good fortune to be traveling with Nat King Cole at the time and Nat said, “You’ve got to hear this guitar player.” And he put this record on, I says, “Wow, who is that?” He said, “Some guy named Joe Pass.” I said, “Joe Pass!”
